newsitem.title: USA: Viacom's Nickelodeon enters Latin America.
newsitem.headline: Viacom's Nickelodeon enters Latin America.

text.p: Viacom Inc's Nickelodeon cable television network for children said Monday it was launching Nickelodeon Latin America, a cable television station for the Latin American market and that it had firm commitments in the region for distribution in two million homes in 16 countries.

Taran Swan, who had been launch director for the service, was named its general manager. She said the decision to go into Latin America with the network rather than just by continuing to license programming came after success in selling its programming in the territory.

"We've been selling our programs in the region for the past six years, and the success we've seen from our programs on other people's networks has been very high," she told Reuters in a telephone interview.

Nickelodeon has an alliance with Artear for distribution in Argentina, Bolivia, Chile, Paraguay and Uruguay. MTV Networks Latin America distributes Nickelodeon in all other Latin American countries and the Caribbean.

Nickelodeon Latin America will be 75 percent first-run programming for the region, with a variety of original and acquired series for children. The company said programming will include live-action, comedy, drama, animation, music, sport and game shows.

Popular Nickeolodeon series such as the animated shows "Doug" and "Rugrats," will be part of the program line-up at launch. "As a general point, the programs that do very, very well in the U.S., a lot of them do very, very well, everywhere," Swan said.
The programming will be transmitted in Spanish, English and Portuguese, and cable operators can choose which language they would like to carry, Nickelodeon spokeswoman Kerry Tatlock said.

Swan said she did not feel it would be a problem for the new network that competition in the Latin American cable market is very tough. "We still believe Nickelodeon is very different and very differentiated, and will be received very well," she said.

Besides the United States, Nickelodeon has dedicated channels in Germany, Britain and Australia. Nickelodeon Latin America will carry children's programming 24 hours per day. Swan said the network currently has no plans to offer a Spanish-language Nickelodeon network in the United States.
